blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
British workplaces are sometimes more traditional than they look. On the surface, teams seem flat and friendly. Everyone uses first names, even the CEO.

Below the surface, hierarchy still matters. Titles, experience and time at the company all carry quiet weight. The trick is to read the room. Use first names, but watch how decisions get made.

Often the most senior person says the least, and then the final word belongs to them. Polite on top, structured underneath — that is the British office.

items.q: How do teams look on the surface?
items.why: "teams seem flat and friendly" — na superfície parecem horizontais e amigáveis.

items.q: What do people call the CEO?
items.why: "Everyone uses first names, even the CEO."

items.q: What still matters below the surface?
items.why: "Below the surface, hierarchy still matters."

items.q: The text suggests that the quiet senior person…
items.why: Inferência: "the final word belongs to them" — quem fala menos pode decidir tudo.

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with…
options: First names show there is no hierarchy.
You should watch how decisions are made.
British offices are polite on top.
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que, apesar dos primeiros nomes, a hierarquia continua existindo.

blocks.instruction: Ouça James explicando ao novo colega quem realmente decide. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Welcome to the team! Let me help you on your first day. You will hear everyone call the CEO 'Richard'. That is normal here. We use first names for everyone.

But do not let that confuse you. We are friendly, yes, but we are not flat. There is a hierarchy under the surface. Richard is the CEO, and his word is final.

In most meetings, only three people really decide. Watch them. They are often quiet. The most senior person in the room usually says the least. Then, at the end, they give the final word.

My advice? Read the room. Do not just read the org chart. Titles matter, but influence matters more. Your line manager may hold more real power than her title shows.

So, be polite, use first names, and watch how decisions are actually made. Do that, and you will do very well here.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does James say about names in the office?
options: They use first names for everyone
They use titles for the CEO
items.why: "We use first names for everyone."

items.q: In most meetings, how many people really decide?
items.why: "only three people really decide."

items.q: What is James's advice to the new joiner?
items.why: "Read the room. Do not just read the org chart."

items.q: James suggests that the quiet person in a meeting is…
items.why: Inferência: "The most senior person in the room usually says the least."

items.q: What does James mean about your line manager?
options: She may have more power than her title shows
Her title shows all her power
items.why: Inferência: "influence matters more" — o cargo esconde o poder real do gerente direto.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The company has a clear hierarchy." A hierarchy is…
options: a group of levels, from top to bottom
items.why: Hierarchy = hierarquia, os níveis do topo até a base.

items.q: "We have a flat structure here." This means…
items.why: Flat structure = estrutura horizontal, poucos níveis entre as pessoas.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Talk to your ___ if you have a problem at work."
items.why: Line manager = gerente direto, a quem você reporta.

items.q: "He is very senior in the team." Senior means…
items.why: Senior = sênior, alto no nível e com mais experiência.

items.q: "You need to read the room in meetings." This means…
options: understand the mood and who decides
read a book in the room
items.why: To read the room = ler o ambiente, entender o clima e quem manda.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem no dia a dia do escritório. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The CEO has to sign off on the plan." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval.

items.q: "We will roll out the new tool next week." To roll out means to…
options: put it in place, step by step
items.why: Roll out = implementar aos poucos.

items.q: "Two people pushed back on the idea." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar.

items.q: "He agreed but never followed through." He…
options: did not finish what he promised
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Try to find out who really decides." To find out means to…
items.why: Find out = descobrir, ficar sabendo.
